data.q_text: Two small conducting spheres of equal radius have charges +10 μC and -20 μC are placed at a distance ‘R’ from each other experience force F1. If they are brought in contact and separated to the same distance, they experience force F2. The ratio of F1 to F2 is :-
data.q_text_hindi: समान त्रिज्या के दो छोटे संवाहक गोले जिनमें +10 μC और -20 μC का आवेश है, जो एक दूसरे से 'R' दूरी पर रखे गए हैं और F1 बल का अनुभव करते हैं। यदि उन्हें संपर्क में लाया जाता है और समान दूरी से पृथक किया जाता है, तब वे F2 बल का अनुभव करते है। F1 से F2 का अनुपात है:-
data.sol_text:
Given:

Charge (q1) = +10 μC

          Charge (q2) = -20 μC

          Distance (d) = R

As we know that

F=kq1q2d2

⇒F1=9×109×(10×10-6)×(20×10-6)R2

When both charges are brought in contact and separated to some distance they experience force F2, then some charge will be on the sphere after contact

Q=q1 + q2 2 = (10×10-6) + (-20×10-6)2= -5×10-6 C

So, the new force will be = F2=kQ2d2

                          ⇒F2=9×109×(5×10-6)2R2

Now the ratio of F1 to F2 is 

⇒F1F2=9×109×(10×10-6)×(20×10-6)R29×109×(5×10-6)2R2=10×(20)5×5

⇒F1F2=81

Therefore option (B) is correct.

data.q_text: Two spherical conductors B and C having equal radii and carrying equal charges in them repel each other with a force F when kept apart at some distance. A third spherical conductor having same radius as that of B but uncharged, is brought in contact with B, then brought in contact with C and finally removed away from both. The new force of repulsion between B and C is
data.q_text_hindi: दो गोलीय चालक B और C (जिनकी त्रिज्यायें समान है तथा समान आवेश वहन करते है) को जब कुछ दूरी पर रखा जाता है तब वे एक दूसरे को बल F से प्रतिकर्षित करते है। B के जैसे समान त्रिज्या का एक तीसरा गोलीय चालक जो अनावेशित है, B के साथ सम्पर्क में लाया जाता है तब C के साथ सम्पर्क में लाया जाता है और अन्त में दोनों से दूर हटा लिया जाता है। B और C के बीच प्रतिकर्षण का नया बल है-
data.sol_text:
Let the spherical conductors B and C have same charge as q. The electric force between them is

F=14πε0q2r2

Here r, being the distance between them. When third uncharged conductor A is brought in contact with

B,then charge on each conductor

qA=qB=qA+qB2 =0+q2=q2

When this conductor A is now brought in contact with C, then charge on each conductor

qA=qC=qA+qC2 =q/2+q2=3q4

Here, electric force acting between B and C is

F'=14πε0qBqCr2 =14πε0q/23q/4r2

=3814πε0q2r2=3F8

data.q_text: A wire of linear charge λ passes through a cuboid of length l, breadth b and height h in such a manner that flux through the cuboid is maximum. The position of wire is now changed so that the flux through the cuboid is minimum. If l > b > h then the ratio of maximum flux to minimum flux will be :
data.q_text_hindi: λ रेखीय आवेश का एक तार, l लम्बाई, b चौड़ाई तथा h ऊँचाई के घनाभ से इस ढंग से गुजरता है कि घनाभ से गुजरने वाला फ्लस्क अधिकतम है। अब तार की स्थिति बदली जाती है ताकि घनाभ से गुजरने वाला फ्लस्क न्यूनतम हो। यदि l > b > h   है, तब अधिकतम फ्लस्क तथा न्यूनतम फ्लस्क का अनुपात होगा:
data.sol_text:
Flux through the cube is maximum when the charge inside it is maximum.

Charge associated with wire  Q=λ l

∴ Q is maximum when l is maximum.

So for maximum flux wire should be placed along the diagonal of cuboid.

Length of diagonal = L2+B2+H2

ϕmax=Qmaxε0=λL2+B2+H2ε0.....(1)

Similarly for minimum flux the wire should be placed along height (h).

     h < b < l

ϕmax=Qmaxε0=λhε0....(2)

From (1) and (2)

ϕmaxϕmin=l2+b2+h2h

∴      (A)

data.sol_text:
Only induced charge on outer surface will redistribute

External electric fields cannot penetrate a closed conductor because of electrostatic shielding. Hence they cannot affect any charges in the interior.

or, The distribution of charge on the outer surface, depends only on the charge outside, and it distributes itself such that the net electric field inside the outer surface due to the charge on the outer surface and all the outer charges is zero.

Similarly, the distribution of charge on the inner surface, depends only on the charges inside the inner surface, and it distributes itself such that the net, electric field outside the inner surface due to the charge on the inner surface and all the inner charges is zero.

 

and, Also, the force on charge inside the cavity is due to the charge on the inner surface.

data.q_text: A positive point charge Q is kept (as shown in the figure) inside a neutral conducting shell whose centre is at C. An external uniform electric field E is applied. Then :
data.q_text_hindi: एक घनात्मक बिन्दु आवेश Q चित्रानुसार एक उदासीन चालकीय कोश (जिसका केन्द्र C पर है) के अन्दर रखा जाता है। एक बाह्य समरूप विद्युत क्षेत्र E आरोपित किया जाता है। तब-
data.sol_text:
As the shell is neutral conducting, and as +Q charge is kept inside it so –ve charge (–Q) will be induced on inner surface of the sphere and +Q charge will be induced on the outer surface of sphere.

Also as E is applied so the +Q & -Q as surface will get deposited as shown in figure below.

 

And a new electric field E1 will be generated inside the sphere opposite in direction to E.

→ Force on Q due to E : F = QE

→ Net force on Q : Fnet = Q (E-E1)

→ Net force on sphere will be zero as it is neutral but there will be a net force on +Q placed inside sphere, so net force acting on Q and conducting shell considered as a system will not be zero.

→ Net force acting on the shell due to E will be zero, as it is a neutral conducting body.

data.sol_text:
Explanations for the correct option

As we know gauss law is used to calculate electric field in cases where there is appropriate symmetry but in this case of dipole there is no symmetry of spherical

Hence we can conclude that it is not convenient to use a spherical gaussian symmetry surface to calculate the electric field due to an electric dipole.

Therefore option (2) is correct

The explanation for the incorrect option

Spherical Gaussian surface is an imaginary surface

Gauss law is not failed in this case so option (1) is incorrect 

Gauss law is more fundamental so option (3) is also incorrect

We know that in the case of people, there is no symmetry, therefore option (4) is also correct

Hence the incorrect options are (1), (3) and (4)

data.q_text: An electric dipole is put in north-south direction in a sphere filled with water. Which statement is correct

data.sol_text:

There can not be a net incoming or outgoing flux. So, options (A) and (B) are discarded.

From Gauss law, total flux passing through the sphere = 0.

So, Option (C) is the correct answer.

data.q_text: When a point charge is placed at h height above the centre, inside the hemisphere the flux passed through circular surface of hemisphere is ϕ. If same point charge is placed below the surface at same distance h from the centre, then what will be flux passed through the circular surface :
data.q_text_hindi: जब एक बिंदु आवेश को केंद्र से h ऊचाई पर अर्द्धगोले के अंदर रखा जाता है तो वृत्तिय फलक से पारित फ्लक्स ϕ है। यदि समान बिंदु आवेश को केंद्र से समान दूरी h पर रखा जाता है तो वृत्तिय फलक से पारित फ्लक्स ज्ञात करों
data.sol_text:
In the first case charge, q is above the curved surface at a height of h from the center 

imagine a spherical surface around it the flux through this surface will be double i.e 2ϕ to that of the hemispherical surface which is ϕ.

Now in the second case imagine the spherical surface and the charge is outside at the same distance from the center as in the first case. So-net flux will be zero since the flux which is entring is also leaving the sphere. So if the flux through the lower half of the hemisphere is -ϕ the flux through the upper half hemisphere will be +ϕ.

So the magnitude of flux will be the same but opposite in the direction in the two cases.

and d=2R

Thus, Esph=-4πR23ρ3×4πϵ0(2R)2=-ρR96ϵ0

Thus, the net electric field is E=ρRϵ014-196=23ρR96ϵ0 thus,

16k=96⇒k=6

data.q_text_hindi: एक आवेशित गोल गेंद के अन्दर स्थिर विद्युत विभव ϕ = ar2 + b से दिया जाता है, जहां r केन्द्र से दूरी तथा a,b स्थिरांक है, तब गेंद के अन्दर आवेश घनत्व है।
data.sol_text:
Given, potential ϕ=ar2+b

So, the electric field is given by,

E=-dϕdr=-2ar+0⇒E=-2ar

Now, from Gauss law, we know

E.A=qε0   (A=Area of the sphere=4πr2)⇒-2ar.4πr2=qε0⇒q=-8πε0ar3

Now, the charge density is given by,

ρ=dqdVWe can rewrite as,ρ=dqdr×drdV

Now, q=-8πε0ar3⇒dqdr=-24πε0ar2And, V=Volume of the sphere=43πr3⇒dVdr=43×3πr2=4πr2

So, substituting these values we get the charge density as,

ρ=dqdr×drdV  =(-24πε0ar2)×14πr2∴ρ=-6ε0a (Answer)

Assume the earth is a conducting medium and the atmosphere around earth is charged with uniform charged density ρ . At 200 m above the surface of the earth, the downward field is 100 Vm−1. The value of ρ is ε 0/k C/m3. Where ε 0 denotes the electric permittivity of free space. Find the value of | k |.
data.q_text_hindi: पृथ्वी की सतह के नजदीक, यहां 150 Vm−1 का नीचे की ओर निर्देशित विद्युत क्षेत्र है। माना पृथ्वी एक चालकीय माध्यम है तथा पृथ्वी के चारो ओर का वायुमण्ड़ल समरूप आवेश घनत्व ρ से आवेशित है। पृथ्वी की सतह से 200 m ऊपर, नीचे की ओर का क्षेत्र 100 Vm−1 है। ρ का मान  ε 0/k C/m3 है। जहां ε 0  मुक्त स्थान की विद्युतशीलता है। | k | का मान ज्ञात करो
data.sol_text:
Let us consider a cylindrical Gaussian surface above the earth with surface area dS and length d.

Now charge on that cylinder is,

q=ρ.dV  =ρ(d×ds)

The earth being a conducting shell, the field inside the earth is zero. So, there is a field only outside.

Now, applying Gauss law,

E2-E1ds=qε0⇒E2-E1ds=ρ×d×dsε0⇒ρ=E2-E1×ε0d⇒ρ=150-100×ε0200=ε04

According to the given data,

ε0k=ε04∴K=4

Answer: The value of k is 4.

data.q_text: When the electric field in air reaches a value of 106 V/m air starts conducting and the charged body discharges. We have a metal ball with a charge of 0.1C. its minimum radius so that it does not discharge is 6x.Find x.
data.q_text_hindi: When the electric field in air reaches a value of 106 V/m air starts conducting and the charged body discharges. We have a metal ball with a charge of 0.1C. its minimum radius so that it does not discharge is 6x.Find x.
data.sol_text:
Given, the charge on the sphere is Q = 0.1 C

Let the radius be R.

We know the field due to this sphere is given by,

E=kQR2=14πε0QR2

Now, the sphere will not discharge until its value is equal to the given value of the electric field in the air i.e. 106 V/m

So, 14πε0QR2≤106⇒9×109×0.1R2≤106⇒R2≥9×109×0.1106≥900⇒R≥30 m∴Rminimum=30 m

Now, according to the given condition:

6x=30

or, x = 5 (Answer)

data.q_text: A spherical shell of charge Q and radius R is broken into 2 parts of charge Q/2 each & made into uniform shells of radius R/2 each. If they are kept such that centres are at a distance of 2R from each other, the work done by external agent is 90x (in J).Find x. Take Q = 200 mC, R = 0.5 m
data.q_text_hindi: आवेश Q तथा R त्रिज्या का एक गोलीय कोश प्रत्येक Q/2  आवेश के 2 भागो मे तोड़ा जाता है तथा प्रत्येक R/2  त्रिज्या के समरूप कोशो मे बना  है। यदि वे इस प्रकार रखे जाते है कि केन्द्र एक दूसरे से 2R दूरी पर है, तब बाह्म एजेन्ट द्वारा किया गया कार्य 90x (J मे) है। तब x ज्ञात करो।
data.sol_text:
The initial potential energy of the hollow spherical shell of radius R and charge Q is given by,

Ui=kQ22R

Finally, each sphere has a radius R/2 and charge Q/2. So, their individual potential energy is,

U1=kQ222R2+kQ222R2   =kQ22R

The interaction energy of these spherical shells is,

U2=kq1q2r   =kQ2Q22R   =kQ28R

So, the final potential energy of the configuration is,

Uf=U1+U2   =kQ22R+kQ28R

The change in potential energy of the system is,Uf-Ui=kQ22R+kQ28R-kQ22R=kQ28R

So, the work done,

W=Uf-Ui=kQ28R

Substituting the values for Q = 200 mC and R = 0.5m, we get

W=9×109×2002×10-128×0.5 J=90 J

So, 90x=90

or, x=1 (Answer)

data.q_text: A spherical conductor of radius 4 cm carries a charge of 1.11 × 10−10 C. distance (in cm) from centre of sphere should a point charge of 4.44 ×10−10 C be placed so that the potential of the conductor becomes 50 V is 4x.Find x. Assume V = 0 at ∞ .
data.q_text_hindi: A spherical conductor of radius 4 cm carries a charge of 1.11 × 10−10 C. distance (in cm) from centre of sphere should a point charge of 4.44 ×10−10 C be placed so that the potential of the conductor becomes 50 V is 4x.Find x. Assume V = 0 at ∞ .
data.sol_text:
The charge on the sphere, Q = 1.11 x 10-10 C

Radius of the sphere, R = 4 cm = 0.04 m.

So, the potential of the sphere due to its own charge is,

V1=kQR   =9×109×(1.11×10-10)0.04 V   ≈25 V

There is one other charge, q = 4.44 x 10-10 C at a distance of 4x cm.

Potential on the sphere due to this charge is,

V2=9×109×4.44×10-10(4x×10-2) V   =9.99×10x V   ≈100x V

Given, the total potential of the sphere is 50V.

∴V1+V2=50 V⇒25+100x=50⇒100x=25∴x=10025=4

Answer: The value of x is 4.

data.q_text: Three large conducting plates are kept close to each other as shown. Now all the three plates A, B, and C are connected by a thin conducting wire. Find the charge (in μC) on left surface of plate A at electrostatic equilibrium.
data.q_text_hindi: तीन बडी चालकीय प्लेटे दिखायेअनुसार एक दूसरे के समीप रखी जाती है। अब सभी तीनो प्लेटो A, B व C को एक पतले चालकीय तार द्वारा जोड़ा जाता है। स्थिर वैघुत साम्यावस्था पर प्लेट A के बायें पृष्ठ पर आवेश (μC मे) ज्ञात करो
data.sol_text:
The outermost charge on the plates will be = (Qtotal)/2 after connecting them with a wire.

Qtotal=(Q-Q+Q)=Q

So, the charge distribution will be like this.

Now the inner charges will be such that, it induces an equal and opposite charge in the next slab surface.

The total charge on both surfaces will give the actual charge of the slab. Like,

For first slab,Q2-x=Q⇒x=Q2Similarly, for the 2nd,-x+y=-Q⇒-Q2+y=-Q⇒y=-Q+Q2=-Q2

So, the final charge distribution will look like the following,

After connecting them with the wires, the middle charges cancel out to be zero and the plates are leftover with Q/2 on the outermost surfaces, which gives the total charge to be Q (conserved).

Now, given Q = 2 µC

So, the charge on the left side of slab A is = Q/2 = 1 µC (Answer)

data.q_text: Two concentric shells have radii R and 2R charges such that their potential 2V and (3/2)V respectively. Now shell B is earthed. What is the new potential of A. Fill ratio of original potential and new potential in OMR sheet.
data.q_text_hindi: Two concentric shells have radii R and 2R charges such that their potential 2V and (3/2)V respectively. Now shell B is earthed. What is the new potential of A. Fill ratio of original potential and new potential in OMR sheet.
data.sol_text:
Let the charges of A and B be qA and qB respectively.

From the first condition, the potential of A:

VA=kqAR+kqB2R

For the sphere B:

VB=kqA2R+kqB2R

Now, the potential difference,

VA-VB=kqAR+kqB2R-kqA2R+kqB2R=kqA2R

So, it depends only on qA. As qA remains the same, the potential difference will also remain the same.

Before earthing B,

VA-VB=2V-32V=V2

After earthing B,

VA'-VB'=VA-VB=V2⇒VA'-0=V2  (As VB'=0 after grounding)∴VA'=V2

The ratio of original potential to the new potential of A is,

VAVA'=2VV2=4

Answer: The ratio is 4.

data.q_text: Three concentric, thin, spherical, metallic shells have radii 1 cm, 2 cm and 4 cm and they are held at potentials 10 V, 0 V and 40 V respectively. Taking the origin at the common centre, calculate the potential (in V) at r = 1.25 cm.
data.q_text_hindi: तीन सकन्द्रीय, पतले, गोलीय धात्विक  कोशो की त्रिज्या 1 cm, 2 cm तथा 4 cm  है तथा वे क्रमशः10 V, 0 V व 40 V विभवो पर रखे जाते है। मूल बिन्दू को उभयनिष्ठ केन्द्र पर लेने पर, r = 1.25 cm पर विभव की गणना (v मे) करो -
data.sol_text:
Given the radius of the shells are, r1 = 1 cm, r2 = 2 cm, and r3 = 4 cm.

Let the charges on the spheres be, q1, q2, and q3 respectively.

Considering the innermost shell:

It is maintained at a potential 10 V.

The potential due to inner shell, V1=kq1r1=kq11×10-2 VThe potential due middle inner shell, V2=kq2r2=kq22×10-2 VThe potential due to outer shell, V3=kq3r3=kq34×10-2 V

Therefore, the total potential on the inner shell,

kq11×10-2+kq22×10-2+kq34×10-2=10 V⇒kq11+kq22+kq34=10×10-2 =0.1 V⇒4q1+2q2+q3=0.4k    ----(1)

Similarly, for the middle shell:

kq12×10-2+kq22×10-2+kq34×10-2=0⇒kq12+kq22+kq34=10×10-2 =0⇒2q1+2q2+q3=0    ----(2)

And for the outer shell, we have

kq14×10-2+kq24×10-2+kq34×10-2=40 V⇒kq14+kq24+kq34=0.4 V⇒q1+q2+q3=1.6k    ----(3)

Substituting equation (1) - (2)

2q1=0.4k⇒q1=0.2k

Substituting equation (2) - (3)

q1+q2=-1.6K⇒0.2k+q2=-1.6K⇒q2=-1.6K-0.2k=-1.8k

Finally, from the equation -(2)

q3=-2q1-2q2⇒q3=-0.4k+3.6k=3.2k

Therefore, the potential at a distance r = 1.25 from the center,

(It is outside the inner shell but inside the two other shells)

V=kq11.25×10-2+kq22×10-2+kq34×10-2  =k1.25×10-20.2k+k2×10-2-1.8k+k4×10-23.2k V  =(16-90+80) V∴V=6 V

Answer: The potential at a distance 1.25 cm is 6 Volt.

data.sol_text:
To find electrostatic pressure:

We know, the electric field produced will be given by,

E=σ2ε0

∴Force, F=QEand Pressure, P=FA=QAσ2ε0=σ22ε0

As soap bubble has two layers, the pressure due to surface tension = 4S/r

According to the question,

σ22ε0=4Sr⇒QA22ε0=4Sr⇒Q24πr222ε0=4SrSubstituting the given value for Q2=12nπε0SV ⇒12nπε0SV4πr222ε0=4Sr⇒6nπ16π2r443πr3=4r    ∵Volume of the sphere, V=43πr3⇒6nπ248π2r=1r⇒n=486=8

Answer: The value of n=8.

data.q_text_hindi: Consider a uniformly charged, insulating sphere of radius R = 5 m. The total amount of charge on the sphere is Q = 6.0 nC. the total electrical flux is 73x Nm2/C through a spherical surface of radius r = 3.0 m that is concentric with the insulating sphere.Find x . Round off to nearest integer.
data.sol_text:
Given, the total charge on the sphere, Q = 6.0 nC;

Radius of the sphere, R = 5 m.

So, charge per unit volume of the sphere is,

ρ=QV=Q43πR3

Charge enclosed by the 3 m radius volume of the sphere,

Qenc=ρ×43π(3)3      =Q43πR3×43π(3)3      =653×(3)3 nC      =1.296 nC = 1.296 ×10-9 C

According to Gauss law, the flux is given by,

ϕ=Qencε0  =1.296×10-98.854×10-12 Nm2/C  ε0=8.854×10-12 C2/Nm2  =146.37 Nm2/C

To match with the given value,

73x=146.37⇒x≃2

Answer: The value of x (rounded off to nearest integer) is 2.

data.q_text: A non-conducting spherical ball of radius R contains a spherically symmetric charge with volume charge density ρ = krn, where r is the distance from the center of the ball and n is a constant. What should be n such that the electric field inside the ball is directly proportional to square of distance from the centre.
data.q_text_hindi: एक R त्रिज्या की अचालक गोलीय गेंद आयतन आवेश घनत्व ρ = krn वाला गोलीय रूप से सममित आवेश रखती है, जहां r गेंद के केन्द्र से दूरी है तथा n एक नियतांक है। n क्या होना चाहिये ताकि गेंद के अन्दर विद्युत क्षेत्र केन्द्र से दूरी के वर्ग के सीधे समानुपाती हो।
data.sol_text:
Considering an elementary surface of thickness dr at a distance r from the center of the ball.

The charge enclosed by the surface is given by,

q=∫ρdV=∫0r(krn)×(4πr2dr)  =4πk∫0rr2+ndr  =4πkr(2+n)+1(2+n)+1r0 ∴q=4πkrn+3n+3

According to Gauss law of electrostatics,

∮E.→dA→=qε0⇒E∫dA=4πkε0rn+3n+3⇒E.4πr2=4πkε0rn+3n+3⇒E=k(n+3)ε0r(n+3)-2=k(n+3)ε0rn∴E∝rn

According to the question,

E∝r2⇒rn=r2∴n=2

Answer: The value of n is 2.

data.q_text: Using Thomson's model of the atom, consider an atom consisting of two electrons, each of charge −e, embedded in a sphere of charge + 2e and radius R. In equilibrium each electron is at distance d from the centre of the atom. The equilibrium separation between electrons are R/x.Find x.
data.q_text_hindi: Using Thomson's model of the atom, consider an atom consisting of two electrons, each of charge −e, embedded in a sphere of charge + 2e and radius R. In equilibrium each electron is at distance d from the centre of the atom. The equilibrium separation between electrons are R/x.Find x.
data.sol_text:
Given, the charge of the sphere is =2e.

The charge density per unit volume of the sphere is given by,

ρ=2e43πR3

Total charge distributed up to distance 'd' from the center is,

q'=ρ×43πd3   =2e43πR3×43πd3∴q'=2ed3R3

Now, the force between this spherical charge and the electrons is,

F1=keq'd2=k×e×2ed3R3d2=2ke2dR3

The force between the two electrons,

F2=k×e×e(2d)2=ke24d2

At equilibrium, F1 = F2

⇒2ke2dR3=ke24d2⇒d3=R38=(R2)3 ∴d=R2

So, the equilibrium separation between the electrons = 2d = R

Hence, Rx=R∴x=1

Answer: The value of x is 1.

data.q_text:
In a linear particle accelerator two large plane uniformly charged are placed parallel to each other as shown in the figure.

Figure also shows variation of potential between planes, A charged particle carrying a charge q = 1.6 × 10-19 C and having mass m = 16 × 10-31 kg is released from rest at x = -10 cm, determine time taken (in ns) by particle to strike the other plane. Neglect relativistic considerations.
data.q_text_hindi:
एक रेखीय कण त्वरक (accelerator ) में एकसमान रूप से आवेशित दो बड़े तल चित्रानुसार एक दूसरे के समानान्तर रखे जाते है।

चित्र तलों के बीच विभव का परिवर्तन भी दिखाता है।  m = 16 × 10-31kg द्रव्यमान तथा q = 1.6 × 10-19 C आवेश वाला एक आवेशित कण x = -10 cm पर विराम से छोड़ा जाता है, दूसरे तल पर टकराने में कण द्वारा लिया समय (ns में) निर्धारित करें। आपेक्षिकीय विचार नगण्य है।
data.sol_text:
Consider in a linear particle accelerator two large plane uniformly charged are placed parallel to each other.

Given that the charged particle carrying a charge q = 1.6 × 10-19 C and having mass m = 16 × 10-31 kg is released from rest at x = -10 cm.

Electric field on particle is E=−ΔVΔx where ∆V is change in potential, ∆x is change in distance

E=−[250−(−250)]20×10−2=−2500 V/m

Acceleration of charge particle: a=qEm where q is charge, E is electric field, m is mass

Then a=1.6×10−19×250016×10−31=2500×1011 m/s2

Distance S=12at2 where a is acceleration, t is time

Then time taken by particle to strike the other plane is:

t=2×Sa

t=2×20×10−22500×1011=4×10−8sec=40 ns

So the time taken (in ns) by particle is 40.

data.q_text: Electric potential at ponit P, r distance away due to a point charge q at A is V volts. If twice of this charge is distributed uniformly on the surface of a hollow sphere of radius 4r with center at point A. The potential at P is now given by vx. Then find the value of x.
data.q_text_hindi: A पर एक बिंदु आवेश q  के कारण r दुरी पर बिंदु P पर विद्युत विभव V  वोल्ट है | यदि इस आवेश के दोगुने (twice) को 4r त्रिज्या के एक खोखले गोले की सतह पर एक सामान रूप से वितरित किया जाता है, जिसका केंद्र बिंदु A पर है| P पर विभव अब vx द्वारा दिया जाता है| तब x का मान ज्ञात करो-
data.sol_text:
Consider an electric potential at point P, r distance away due to a point charge q at A is V volts.

Potential at P due to point charge is V=Kqr where K is constant, q is charge, r is distance

Here the radius of hollow sphere R=4r.

So, point P is inside the hollow sphere.

Now the potential at P will be:

Vin=Vsurface=K(2q)4r=Kq2r=V2

So if the potential at P is now given by vx, then the value of x is 2.

data.q_text: A thick shell with inner radius R and outer radius 3R has a uniform charge density ρ. It has a spherical cavity of radius R as shown in figure. The electric field at the centre of the cavity is nρRmε0, where m and n are co-prime numbers. Find value of m+n.
data.q_text_hindi: आंतरिक त्रिज्या R और बाहरी त्रिज्या 3R वाले एक मोटे कोश में एकसमान आवेश घनत्व ρ है। इसमे त्रिज्या R का एक गोलाकार गुहिका (cavity) है जैसा कि चित्र में दिखाया गया है। गुहिका के केंद्र में विधुत क्षेत्र nρRmε0 है, जहाँ m और n सह-अभाज्य संख्याँए है। m + n का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
data.sol_text:
We can consider the electric field at center to be a sum of electric fields due to complete shell of charge density ρ if it did not have any cavity, and due to a sphere of cavity of charge density −ρ. Due to symmetry, the electric at center due to former is zero. The later produces an electric field at center towards right given as-

E=14πϵ0qr2

=14πϵ0ρ(43πR3)(2R)2 ​

=ρR12ϵ0​

⇒n=1 & m=12

⇒n+m=13

data.q_text: Two concentric spherical metal shells have radii R and 2R respectively. The inner shell has charge Q and the outer shell has charge -2Q. Potential at the centre of the combination is V1. Now the outer shell is grounded and potential at the centre becomes V2. If V2-V1=x·Q16πε0R, then find x.
data.q_text_hindi: दो संकेद्रित गोलाकार धातु के कोश जिनकी त्रिज्याएँ क्रमशः R और 2R है। आंतरिक कोश मे आवेश Q है और बाहरी कोश मे आवेश–2Q हैं। संयोजन के केंद्र पर विभव V1 है। अब बाहरी कोश भुसंपर्कित है और केंद्र पर विभव V2 हो जाता है। यदि V2-V1=x·Q16πε0R तब x ज्ञात कीजिए।
data.sol_text:
V1=KQR+K(-2Q)2R=0

V2=KQR+K(-Q)2R=KQ2R=Q8πε0R

⇒ x=2

data.sol_text:
Cavity can be treated as a combination of +ρ and -ρ. However field, due to ' -ρ' at the centre of cavity is zero.

⇒ Net field at the centre of cavity is simply due to +ρ. Use Gauss' law

E×4π(2R)2=ρ×43π(2R)3-R3ε0

⇒E=7ρR12ε0⇒n=7
